result.reason: The passage contains the full Rav Naḥman/Shmuel teaching including both the roof-adjacent-to-courtyard rule (four amot) and the between-rooftops distinction, which candidate 0's prose explicitly discusses as a unified teaching before the subsequent analysis in candidates 1 and 2.

The passage directly discusses the Gemara's reasoning about the purpose of the ten-tefachim partition (hezek reiyah vs. trespass vs. animals) and concludes it is for trespass prevention, which is precisely what the 'Trespass Concern' section's prose describes and analyzes.

The passage directly discusses the case of a courtyard higher than a neighbor's roof and the question of whether 'ein nizkakin lo' means no obligation at all or only exemption from four cubits, which is precisely what the 'Higher Yard Exemption' section's prose analyzes in detail.

Both items — Rav Ḥisda's ruling and the supporting baraita — are explicitly discussed together in candidate 1's prose ('Rav Chisda Opinion'), which mentions both elyon mesayeya milimata uboneh and the baraita citation tanyah kevata de-Rav Chisda, matching the content of items 1 and 2 precisely.

Both items describe the narrative of the two tenants — the lower story collapsing and the upper tenant refusing to cooperate — which is precisely what heading 1 ('Upper Tenant Refusal') discusses in its prose, including the specific dialogue about crawling in and out on one's belly.
The passage directly states Rav Ḥama's ruling about the ten-handbreadth threshold and the lower tenant's domain claim, which is precisely what the 'Ten Tefachim Threshold' prose section discusses.

The passage explicitly discusses the stipulation between parties and the consequence of rebuilding when such a stipulation exists, which directly matches the 'Stipulation & Heikhal' section's prose about prior stipulations triggering rebuilding obligations.

The passage directly discusses Rav Nachman's standard of 'as people normally live' and Rav Huna's Meḥoza bundle example, which is precisely what the 'Normal Usage Standards' prose section describes and analyzes.

Both items together form the extended negotiation between the builder and neighbor about window solutions, which is precisely what heading 0's prose describes in detail, including all the objections and counteroffers culminating in the neighbor's refusal to be troubled — with Rav Ḥama's ruling at the end of item 2 being the closing line of that same case, already anticipated in heading 0's prose summary.
The passage directly addresses the 'hainu hach' question and the storehouse/straw-and-wood answer, which is explicitly discussed in the Rav Chama Ruling prose.

All nine items form one continuous discussion about the two brothers who divided their estate (hall and garden), including the challenge from the vineyard baraita, the airspace resolution, the 'name only' argument, and the Shmuel/Neharde'a principle — all of which are covered in the 'Brothers' Division' prose.

The passage describes exactly the case discussed in 'Keep Original Shtar' prose: orphans holding a shtar against which a tavra (receipt) was produced, and Rav Chama's ruling to neither collect nor tear up the document.

Both items — Ravina's ruling (halakha follows Rav Chama except the receipt case) and Mar Zutra's dissent (even the receipt case follows Rav Chama) — are precisely the content described in the 'Final Psak Decision' prose, which quotes both positions verbatim and explains their reasoning.
